newsitem.title: UK: Mideast/South Korea VLCCs continue to firm.
newsitem.headline: Mideast/South Korea VLCCs continue to firm.

text.p: Very large crude carrier (VLCC) rates from the Middle East to South Korea continued to firm on Thursday on a lack of available tonnage, brokers said.

The 265,000 tonne New Vision was said fixed at W75 Mideast/Onsan for Ssanyong, up some five points from Wednesday. There were also signs that voyages west were firming. One broker said the W59 done earlier in the week for a UKC voyage now looked "quite cheap and it could now achieve a bit more." A Mideast/South Africa fixture was also done at a high number -- the Berge Duke at W74.5 for Vela.

About three ultra-large vessels (ULCCs) were also fixed from the Middle East, including the world's largest tanker, the Jahre Viking, which was done at W51.5 for 550,000 tonnes Ras Tanura/Brazil for Exxon. But brokers said rates for ULCCs remained flat from earlier in the week.

West Africa/U.S. Gulf VLCCs were little changed at W65 and brokers said the North Sea/U.S. Atlantic coast market was notionally steady around W60. The 80,000 tonne (Aframax) inter-U.K./Cont market fell further to W95 from W107.5 on Wednesday and after hitting around W140 last week.
"There are too many vessels with some attracting six offers," one broker said.
The Med Aframax market was sluggish with vessels fixed in a range W105-115, and brokers said the disappearance of eight to 10 vessels from this sector had not so far been enough to push rates up.
Rates for Med and West Africa/U.S. 130,000 tonne vessels (Suezmaxes) were steady at W95.
U.K./Cont fuel oil remained firm at W250 for 25,000 tonne stems as strong demand continued from the Baltic, but in the Med it languished at around W200.
Western hemisphere rates were little changed, with 70,000 tonne crude cargoes at W210/215 and 50,000 tonne fuel oil stems at W205.
